title.narrative: Multisectorial Response to projected Extreme Climate Events in Southern Ethiopia – South Omo; Woredas of Dasenech and Bena Tsemay

description.narrative: ltpgtDoctors with Africa CUAMM proposes to urgently respond and address the immediate lifesaving needs of the most vulnerable women, children, IDPs and host communities affected by climate changes in the most southern part of South Omo Region, Ethiopia. ltbrgtIn South Omo, Ethiopia, a severe humanitarian crisis has recently emerged due to La Niña atmospheric events, causing seasonal drought and flooding. In the Dasenech district, over 90% of the population is displaced and facing acute food insecurity. Moreover, malnutrition rates are alarmingly high, with 16% of children under five suffering from global acute malnutrition. Access to health services is critically limited, further endangering vulnerable populations. Urgent interventions are needed to address nutrition and health for affected host communities and IDPs.ltbrgtThe organization has a long-term presence in the operational zones, including an ongoing project in Maternal And Child Health in Kuniz district (will be terminated on January 2026) and a new project starting in December 2024 in Jinka, on nutrition and health. ltbrgtThe proposed project can be considered as a scale-up intervention, which targets two woreda, namely Bena Tsmei and Dasenech, in South Omo region. ltbrgtThe project aims to support 96,232 people affected by recent flooding—approximately 51% of whom are female and 50% are children under 18—following a period of drought that led to the establishment of numerous IDP camps. The initiative will focus on two main pillars of the interventions managed by the Organization: (1) the health sector component (50%) seeks to strengthen the community-level health system by providing mobile clinics to 12 remote communities and 5 IDP camps. At the peripheral level, the project aims to strengthen and support 9 health centers in delivering basic health care, providing equipment, drugs and trainings, and will enable ambulance services to manage up to 360 emergencies. At the district level, efforts will be made to enhance the health system's capacity to prevent and respond to outbreaks through supervision, provision of equipment, and coordination meetings. (2) On the other hand, the nutrition component (50%) aims to address the nutritional emergency in the area through a Cash Transfer program for 350 households, food cooking demonstrations for over 450 women, and support for the health system in providing nutritional components at 9 health centers and through mobile activities in the communities. Moreover, two courses on the most updated guidelines on nutrition should update and refresh around 120 HCWs of the two districts. ltbrgtActivities will be integrated with other organizations (e.g., coordinating with VSF, which implements WASH and agriculture components in the same emergency response), as well as with local and national woredas and clusters, through the project's management staff. Human resources will be assigned to specific roles and responsibilities, including a national nutrition expert and two clinical team leaders for the mobile clinics, who will ensure the quality of their components. An international expert will oversee the quality of the health care strengthening efforts.ltbrgtThe total value of the intervention is $499,786.26, with activities set to begin in November 2024 and continue for a duration of six months.ltbrgtlt/pgt
